Jesus told the disciples to wait for the promise of the Father. Why is waiting on God sometimes part of obedience?
Jesus says you will receive power and be his witnesses. Where is your "Jerusalem," the place you start?
The angels asked why they stood looking into the sky. How does Jesus' return shape how you live now?
The believers devoted themselves to prayer together. What could praying together do in your pasture?
The Spirit came and people heard of God's mighty works in their own languages. What does this show about God's heart for all nations?
Peter preached that God raised Jesus and made him Lord and Christ. Which part of Peter's message stands out to you?
The crowd asked, "What shall we do?" How would you answer someone asking that today?
The early church devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread and prayer. Which of these do you most need?
Peter said, "I have no silver and gold, but what I do have I give to you." What do you have from Jesus that you can give?
Peter gave all the credit to Jesus' name. How can you point to Jesus rather than yourself?
Peter invites them to repent so that times of refreshing may come. What refreshing do you need from God?
God sent Jesus to bless you by turning you from wickedness. What does God want to turn you from?
Peter boldly said there is salvation in no one else. Why does Peter speak so confidently about Jesus?
The leaders saw Peter and John had been with Jesus. What would people notice about you from time spent with Jesus?
The believers prayed for boldness, not for safety. What would you pray in their place?
No one among them was in need because they shared. How could you share what you have?
Ananias and Sapphira lied about their giving. Why does God care so much about honesty?
Many were added to the Lord as the apostles served. What does God use to draw people to himself?
Peter said, "We must obey God rather than men." Where does this choice show up in your life?
They rejoiced to suffer dishonour for the name. How can that kind of joy be possible?
The apostles chose seven to serve so that the word could keep spreading. What does this teach about everyone having a part?
They looked for people "full of the Spirit and of wisdom." How could you grow in both?
Stephen was full of grace and power, and his face was like an angel's. What does a Spirit-filled life look like under pressure?
Stephen retells how God was with Joseph in Egypt. How has God been with you in hard places?
Israel kept turning back in their hearts. Where are you tempted to turn back?
Stephen said the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands. Where is God to be found?
Stephen prayed, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." What does his prayer teach you about forgiveness?
The scattered believers preached wherever they went. How might God use your hard circumstances to spread the gospel?
Simon thought he could buy God's gift. Why can't God's gifts be bought?
Philip asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?" Who has helped you understand the Bible?
The Ethiopian went on his way rejoicing. What brings you joy about the gospel?
Jesus said to Saul, "Why are you persecuting me?" What does it mean that Jesus takes the treatment of his people personally?
Ananias was afraid but obeyed. When has God asked you to do something that scared you?
Barnabas stood by Saul when others feared him. Who could you encourage or stand beside?
Tabitha was full of good works and acts of charity. How could your kindness show Jesus?
Cornelius was a devout man who prayed and gave. What do his prayers and generosity teach you?
God told Peter, "What God has made clean, do not call common." Who might you be tempted to see as an outsider?
Peter said God shows no partiality. How does this change how you treat others?
The Spirit fell on the Gentiles as they listened. What does this show about who the gospel is for?
The church glorified God that he had given repentance to the Gentiles. How do you respond when God works in unexpected people?
In Antioch the disciples were first called Christians. What does that name mean to you?
Barnabas saw the grace of God and was glad. Where can you see and celebrate God's grace in others?
The disciples each gave according to their ability. How could you help those in need?
Peter was in prison, but the church prayed earnestly for him. Who could you pray for earnestly?
Peter slept peacefully the night before his trial. What gave him such peace?
The believers were praying for Peter but were amazed when he knocked. Why are we sometimes surprised when God answers?
Herod did not give God the glory, but the word of God increased. What does this show about who is really in charge?
The church was worshipping and fasting when the Spirit spoke. How can you make space to hear God?
Paul traced God's story from Israel to Jesus. How does knowing the whole story help you understand Jesus?
Through Jesus forgiveness of sins is proclaimed. What does forgiveness mean to you today?
The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit even amid opposition. Where does joy come from in hard times?
Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly and the city was divided. What does boldness in faith look like for you?
Paul and Barnabas refused to be worshipped and pointed to the living God. How can you redirect praise to God?
Paul said, "Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God." How does this prepare you?
They reported all that God had done with them. What has God done in your life that you could tell?
Peter said we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus. Why is grace, not rules, the heart of the gospel?
James saw that God was calling people from the nations. How does God's plan include everyone?
The letter brought encouragement and the believers rejoiced. How could you encourage someone this week?
Paul and Barnabas disagreed sharply, yet God kept working. What does this teach about handling disagreements?
The Spirit closed some doors and opened another. How have you seen God guide through closed doors?
The Lord opened Lydia's heart to pay attention. Who could you pray for to have an open heart?
Paul and Silas sang hymns in prison at midnight. What helps you praise God in dark times?
The jailer asked, "What must I do to be saved?" How would you answer him?
The believers were accused of turning the world upside down. What would it look like for the gospel to change things around you?
The Bereans examined the Scriptures daily. How can you read the Bible with that kind of eagerness?
Paul said God is not far from each one of us. Where have you sensed God near?
Some mocked, some wanted to hear more, some believed. How do you respond when people react differently to faith?
The Lord told Paul, "Do not be afraid, but go on speaking." What would you say if you weren't afraid?
God protected Paul as he promised. How have you seen God keep his promises?
Priscilla and Aquila quietly helped Apollos understand more accurately. How can you help someone grow in faith?
These disciples had not heard of the Holy Spirit. What does the Spirit's presence mean in your life?
Many burned their magic books when they believed. What might you need to give up as you follow Jesus?
The silversmiths opposed the gospel because it threatened their business. Where does faith clash with money?
Eutychus fell from the window during a long talk and was raised. What does this story show about God's care?
Paul said he did not hold back anything that was profitable. What does it mean to finish your course faithfully?
Paul committed the elders to God and to the word of his grace. Who could you commit to God in prayer?
Paul quoted Jesus: "It is more blessed to give than to receive." Where could you be generous this week?
The believers said, "Let the will of the Lord be done." When have you had to accept God's will?
Paul tried to keep peace with Jewish believers. How can you avoid needless offence for others' sake?
A mob seized Paul, yet God protected him. How have you seen God protect in chaos?
Paul told his story of meeting Jesus. How would you tell your own story of coming to faith?
Ananias said Paul would be a witness to everyone of what he had seen and heard. What have you seen and heard?
Paul's mention of the Gentiles enraged the crowd. Why does God's love for outsiders offend some?
Paul said, "I have lived my life before God in all good conscience." How do you keep a clear conscience?
The Lord stood by Paul and said, "Take courage." Where do you need his courage today?
God used Paul's nephew to foil a plot. How does God work through ordinary people?
Paul said he always took pains to have a clear conscience toward God and man. What does that look like for you?
Felix grew afraid when Paul spoke of righteousness and self-control, and put it off. What might you be putting off with God?
Paul stood calmly before his accusers and appealed to Caesar. What does his calm teach you?
Festus summed up the gospel as about "a certain Jesus, who was dead, but whom Paul asserted to be alive." Why is that the centre?
Paul said he was not disobedient to the heavenly vision. What has God called you to?
Jesus sent Paul to open eyes and turn people from darkness to light. Who do you long to see turn to the light?
Agrippa asked, "Would you persuade me to be a Christian?" How do you share faith with honesty and respect?
They lost all hope in the storm. When have you felt that way?
Paul said, "Take heart, for I have faith in God that it will be exactly as I have been told." What promise can you hold onto?
Paul gave thanks and broke bread before everyone in the storm. How can gratitude steady others?
Everyone was brought safely to land, just as God said. What does this show about God's faithfulness?
Paul shook off the viper and was unharmed. What does this show about God's protection?
Paul served the people of Malta by praying and healing. How can you bless the place you are in?
Paul thanked God and took courage when he saw the believers. Who gives you courage?
Paul kept proclaiming the kingdom "with all boldness and without hindrance." How can you keep sharing faith in your situation?
